gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-hind-siliguri: Ethnocentric hits fast and aggressive, its letters pushed apart by wide tracking over big, smooth bowls. Hind Siliguri brings a flat, constant line weight that makes the plain sans feel approachable next to all that stretched-out attitude.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-hind-vadodara: Loud, wide and in a hurry. Ethnocentric is built for the big gesture, with short ascenders over huge bowls, while Hind Vadodara does the quieter job, with spacious openings in its rounded letters and tall-bowled e and a.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-huninn: Huninn reads modern and tidy, its lowercase rising close to cap height and its s terminals held clear of the body. And Ethnocentric stretches out above it, spaced wide and fast, so the heading shouts while the text simply gets on with it.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight reads smooth and modern, like bent tubing with tiny ascenders. Ethnocentric is best at slamming out wide, aggressive display letters, whereas the sans-serif body is best at staying uniform in stroke and tucked-in curves all the way through.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-karla: Karla reads modern and friendly, with a gaping c opening and a middle band so tall the line looks stocky. Its sturdy build is the pair's strongest quality against Ethnocentric.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-kedebideri: Ethnocentric arrives fast and aggressive, with short ascenders over big bowls and generous spacing between letters. And Kedebideri, a sans-serif with a skyward x-height and inviting rounded forms, gives that attitude a friendly, open counterweight.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-khula: Modern and unfussy, Khula has a tall midsection like a squat brush-pen belly and curves that hold their mouths open. Ethnocentric does best at speed and aggression with wide-set letters, while the sans-serif body does best at staying approachable.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-krub: Krub reads contemporary, with a pronounced x-height and curves that leave loops unfinished. Ethnocentric is best at fast, widely spaced display punch, while the sans-serif body is best at quietly carrying text.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-kufam: Ethnocentric's wide tracking pushes its letters apart, giving a fast and aggressive heading with big bowls and low ascenders. And Kufam keeps every stroke one track width like a neon tube, so a longer stretch of the plain sans looks clean, with open e curves.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-lexend: Approachable at heart, Lexend has outsized lowercase and open jaws on every curve, with a thickness that never shifts around bends. Ethnocentric adds speed and aggression on top, so the pair feels fast then friendly.
